issues.body: The design first states that termArg distinguishes str by coercing it to a NamedNode, but step 3 then classifies a string-literal constant as a syntactic form that cannot produce a graph name and requires rejecting it at generation time. Those statements are incompatible: under the described existing evaluation semantics, a str expression does produce the NamedNode variant admitted by GraphName. Implementing the proposed check would reject valid quad-emission grammars rather than merely reject out-of-space graph terms.
issues.fix_hint: Remove string-literal constants from the statically rejected forms, or explain and specify a graph-slot-specific semantic change that intentionally disables the existing str-to-NamedNode coercion. Add a positive generator/runtime test for the chosen string case so the compile-time filter is demonstrated to be acceptance-preserving; keep literal(..) and tt(..) as negative cases.
issues.title: Compile-time graph check rejects a form that termArg turns into a named node

verdict.summary: Round 2 fixes both prior findings: it adds runtime.inc.rs to the gen-rs touch-point inventory and makes the graph-name value space a real invariant through a closed GraphName type plus fallible emission-time conversion, with negative and behavioral tests in both backends. However, the newly specified compile-time check contradicts the document's own account of termArg(): it rejects string-literal graph expressions even though termArg coerces str to NamedNode. That would reject an expression whose evaluated value is in the graph-name value space, so the design is not yet correct as written.
